content.content:
60	IBM Systems Journal 24(2), 1985, pp. 79–90) is the lightest classic
61	per-activity frame: Entry criteria, Task set, Validation conditions, eXit
62	criteria per activity cell, composable by chaining, with no ordering engine.
63	(Corrected: the original expansion is Validation, not Verification; both
64	renderings circulate in CMM-lineage secondary literature. A free scan exists at
65	bitsavers.org despite the IBM Systems Journal paywall.) The frame places
66	validation conditions inside the activity definition cell itself.
67	
68	OMG Essence 1.2 (SEMAT; OMG formal/18-10-02, 2018; omg.org/spec/Essence —
69	1.2 remains the current formal version; Essence 2.0 is still an in-process
70	beta, its beta 2 published March 2026 and not yet formally published as of
71	August 2026, per the OMG specification page — corrected) defines
72	progress and health rather than workflow: Alphas (essential trackable concerns)
73	with ordered named states, each state carrying a short qualitative checklist;
74	activities whose completion criteria are expressed in terms of alpha states and
75	work-product levels of detail — a definition-level termination semantic
76	requiring no engine; competencies with five levels; practice/method
77	composition; a card presentation format.
78	
79	CMMI contributes a structural trichotomy: in CMMI for Development V1.3
80	(CMU/SEI-2010-TR-033, 2010) goals are required components, practices are
81	expected, and subpractices/example work products are informative — appraisal
82	targets goal achievement, not practice performance; CMMI V3.0 (ISACA, 2023)
83	recasts this as practice areas with intent and value statements and
84	evolutionary practice-group levels. ITIL v3 (Service Design, 2011 ed., Cabinet
85	Office/TSO) documents every process in one fixed section skeleton (purpose/
86	objectives, scope, value, policies, activities, triggers/inputs/outputs/
87	interfaces, CSFs with nested KPIs, risks), and ITIL 4 (AXELOS, 2019; 34
88	practice guides) does the same for practices — success factors and metrics
89	nested under the definition.
90	
91	Notation standards exist but describe flow or I/O, not construction quality:
92	BPMN 2.0 (OMG formal/2011-01-03; ISO/IEC 19510:2013, which is technically BPMN
93	2.0.1) with its Descriptive vs Analytic vs Common Executable conformance
94	sub-classes; CMMN 1.0/1.1 (OMG, 2014; Marin, arXiv:1608.05011) — declarative
95	case plans with sentries (entry/exit criteria), milestones, and discretionary
96	items, addressed to case work whose activities cannot be fully pre-sequenced;
97	IDEF0 (NIST FIPS PUB 183, 1993, withdrawn as a federal
98	standard in 2008; IEEE 1320.1-1998; ISO/IEC/IEEE 31320-1:2012) with its
99	Input/Control/Output/Mechanism arrow typing; and PMBOK 6th ed. ITTOs (PMI,
100	2017), which the PMBOK 7th ed. (2021) itself dropped from the core. ISO/IEC
101	24744:2014 (SEMDM) models method-level and endeavor-level views of one concept
102	via powertypes; this survey found no practitioner process corpus written in it
103	comparable to the 15288/12207 corpus, the application literature encountered
104	being academic method-engineering work (observation from this research pass,
105	not a cited measurement).
106	
107	### 1.2 Role definition formats
108	
109	OMG SPEM 2.0 (formal/2008-04-01, April 2008; omg.org/spec/SPEM/2.0) draws a
110	hard structural line between Method Content — reusable Role Definitions
111	(skills, responsibilities), Task Definitions, Work Product Definitions, typed
112	Guidance including checklists — and Process, which arranges content occurrences
113	into lifecycles. A full knowledge base of role/task/artifact definitions can be
114	maintained without ever creating a process. Eclipse EPF Composer
115	(projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.epf; archived, last release 2018)
116	implements the split in tooling: method plugins publish role/task/work-product/guidance pages
117	as a browsable static site, no engine. RUP (Kruchten, The Rational Unified
118	Process: An Introduction, 3rd ed., Addison-Wesley, 2003, ch. 3) is the
119	ancestor form: roles carry responsibilities plus required competencies, and
120	every artifact has exactly one responsible role.
121	
122	The Scrum Guide (Schwaber & Sutherland, November 2020, scrumguides.org) defines
123	roles as short accountability lists — 4–8 bullets of what the holder is
124	answerable for, not task scripts.
125	
126	Responsibility assignment across roles has its own established forms, distinct
127	from the definition containers above. The responsibility assignment matrix
128	(RAM) and its common type, the RACI chart, are carried in the PMBOK Guide: a
129	RAM is "a grid that shows the project resources assigned to each work
130	package"; a RACI chart is "a common type of RAM that uses responsible,
131	accountable, consult, and inform statuses to define the involvement of
132	stakeholders in project activities" (PMI, PMBOK Guide, 6th ed., 2017, §9.1
133	data-representation tools and glossary — definitions confirmed via
134	PMI-affiliated PMP literature quoting the Guide, the Guide itself being
135	paywalled; ancestry in the Linear Responsibility Chart, Cleland & King,
136	Systems Analysis and Project Management, McGraw-Hill, 1968). The matrix
137	crosses work items (rows) with roles (columns), one involvement status per
138	cell. The one-Accountable-per-row rule — exactly one A per deliverable — is
139	stated as hard doctrine throughout PMI-affiliated practitioner literature,
140	though the PMBOK glossary itself defines only the four statuses; the R-A-C-I
141	lettering has no documented originator (folklore attributions to GE/1950s are
142	unverified). Practitioner criticism records recurring failure modes: multiple
143	As dissolving accountability, R/A conflation, team-level unnamed assignments,
144	consulted-list bloat, and shelfware charts drafted once and never consulted
145	(e.g. tallyfy.com/raci-matrix — criticism in circulation, not authority).
146	Letter-set variants extend the cell vocabulary on the same skeleton: RASCI
147	(S = Support, splitting doer from helper), RACI-VSL (V = Verifier against
148	acceptance criteria, S = Signatory), CAIRO (O = explicitly Omitted), RACIQ
149	(Q = Quality review), PARIS (variant inventory per the Wikipedia RAM article,
150	en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsibility_assignment_matrix). A decision-rights
151	fork re-targets the matrix from tasks to decisions: Bain's RAPID — Recommend /
152	Agree / Perform / Input / Decide, "one person who must decide — the single
153	point of accountability", plus a four-locus taxonomy of decision bottlenecks
154	(Rogers & Blenko, "Who Has the D?", HBR 84(1), January 2006;
155	bain.com/insights/who-has-the-d/) — and DACI — Driver / Approver /
156	Contributors / Informed, one Approver, splitting process ownership (Driver)
157	from final authority (Approver) (Atlassian Team Playbook,
158	atlassian.com/team-playbook/plays/daci; the commonly repeated Intuit-1980s
159	origin is an unverified secondary attribution).
160	
161	Holacracy constitutionalizes the role definition itself (Holacracy
162	Constitution v5.0, holacracy.org/constitution/5-0; source text at
163	github.com/holacracyone/Holacracy-Constitution, CC BY-SA 4.0; Robertson,
164	Holacracy, Henry Holt, 2015). Its §1.1 defines a Role as a descriptive name
165	plus three optional typed parts: Purpose ("a capacity, potential, or goal that
166	the Role will pursue or express"), Domains (things the role exclusively
167	controls and regulates as its property), and Accountabilities ("ongoing
168	activities the Role will manage and enact in service of others"), by
169	documented HolacracyOne convention phrased as gerunds. Role and person are
170	strictly separated: a person filling a role is its Role Lead (§1.2), assigned
171	by a Circle Lead (§1.4.1), many-to-many in both directions. Definitions change
172	only through the governance process (Article 5): proposals must be grounded in
173	a concrete tension with an example (§5.3.1), are processed by integrative
174	decision-making (§5.4.5), and objections must pass defined validity tests
175	(§5.3.2–5.3.3); amendments are recorded, giving the role set an audit trail.
176	A documented exit exists: Medium abandoned Holacracy in 2016, reporting that
177	"the act of codifying responsibilities in explicit detail hindered a proactive
178	attitude and sense of communal ownership" (Doyle, "Management and Organization
179	at Medium", Medium blog, 4 March 2016).
180	
181	Team Topologies (Skelton & Pais, IT Revolution, 2019; concept definitions at
182	teamtopologies.com/key-concepts) types teams — stream-aligned, enabling,
183	complicated-subsystem, platform — and types the relationship between any two
184	teams into three interaction modes: collaboration ("working together for a
185	defined period of time to discover new things"), X-as-a-Service ("one team
186	provides and one team consumes something 'as a Service'"), and facilitating
187	("one team helps and mentors another team"), with a designed evolution —
188	collaboration is deliberately time-bounded and expected to decay into
189	X-as-a-Service as interfaces stabilize. It is the one surveyed form that types
190	role-to-role interaction rather than involvement in a deliverable.
191	
192	In current agent practice, the Claude Code subagent definition
193	(code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) is a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter
194	is the delegation and capability contract (required name and description;
195	optional tools/disallowedTools, model, maxTurns, skills preload list, memory
196	scope) and whose body is the role's standing system prompt. The shop already
197	uses this container for lead-po and lead-architect.
198	
199	### 1.3 Artifact / document-type schema formats
200	
201	ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289:2019 (Content of life-cycle information items, 4th ed.;
202	earlier editions 2011/2015/2017; iso.org/standard/74909.html) is the
203	established meta-format: every information item is classified as one of seven
204	generic document types — description, plan, policy, procedure, report, request,
205	specification — each generic type carrying generic content requirements, and
206	each named item carrying specific required-content clauses. It is explicitly
207	medium-independent, and its mapping tables tie information items to the
208	12207/15288 processes that produce and consume them.
209	
210	RUP artifacts (Kruchten 2003, ch. 3) ship with templates and checkpoints —
211	per-artifact review checklists attached to the artifact definition. The 2020
212	Scrum Guide pairs every artifact with exactly one commitment (Product Backlog →
213	Product Goal, Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal, Increment → Definition of Done);
214	the DoD is "a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets
215	the quality measures required for the product," with a defined consequence:
216	non-conforming work returns to the Product Backlog. Microsoft Prompty
217	(prompty.ai/core-concepts/file-format; microsoft/prompty) demonstrates a
218	schema-validated asset format whose frontmatter declares inputs, outputs, and
219	per-input sample/default data. The MCP resources primitive (Model Context
220	Protocol spec 2025-06-18) standardizes inclusion-decision metadata on context
221	artifacts: audience, priority 0.0–1.0, lastModified.
222	
223	Two traditions govern how document kinds themselves are derived and bounded.
224	DITA 1.3 (OASIS Standard, 17 December 2015; Errata 02, 2018;
225	docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3) types every topic as one of a small set of
226	information types sharing one structural envelope (title + prolog metadata +
227	body): the base triad concept / task / reference, extended in the 1.3
228	technical-content set by glossaryEntry (introduced in DITA 1.1 — corrected: an
229	earlier research pass dated it to 1.3) and troubleshooting (the type actually
230	new in 1.3). Typing exists to "keep documentation focused and modular"; mixing
231	information types within one topic is the named anti-pattern; and a document's
232	root element must be <topic> or a specialization, <map> or a specialization,
233	or <dita> (corrected: <dita> is also a permitted root). Maps — separate
234	documents that "organize topics and other resources into structured
235	collections" — carry hierarchy, inter-topic relationships, and key-resolution
236	context, so organization is fully separated from content. DITA's
237	specialization architecture (archSpec "Specialization"; the definition sits in
238	the spec's terminology section) is a governed derivation mechanism: "defining
239	new element or attribute types as a semantic refinement of existing element or
240	attribute types". Every specialized type declares its full ancestry (@class),
241	so a processor that knows only the base type can still process the derived one
242	(generic fallback); vocabulary compatibility between documents is decidable
243	(@domains); each type is declared in exactly one vocabulary module; and
244	constraint modules restrict an existing type's content model as a distinct,
245	lighter operation than creating a new type (fallback and constraint rules
246	specified in adjacent archSpec sections).
247	
248	Diátaxis (Procida, diataxis.fr; authorship per the site's colophon — the
249	homepage does not name the author) classifies on an axis orthogonal to
250	15289's content genres: by the user's need at the moment of use. Two axes —
251	action/cognition crossed with acquisition/application ("at work" vs "at
252	study") — generate exactly four types: tutorial, how-to guide, reference,
253	explanation. The type determines "documentation content (what to write),
254	style (how to write it) and architecture (how to organise it)"; the named
255	failure mode is the blurring or collapse of the forms into one document,
256	which the site prescribes keeping apart (an each-document-serves-one-type
257	rule in paraphrase — the site states it as failure-mode avoidance, not in
258	those words). Adjacent: arc42 (Hruschka & Starke, arc42.org, in practice
259	since 2005) is a fixed 12-section skeleton for one composite artifact kind —
260	the architecture description — with explicit tailoring permission and a
261	decision-record slot (its section 9) embedding the ADR kind by reference; and
262	docs-as-code (Write the Docs, writethedocs.org/guide/docs-as-code; Gentle,
263	Docs Like Code) names the substrate practice — documentation in plain-text
264	markup under version control, peer-reviewed via the code-review mechanism,
265	gated by automated tests in CI — while deliberately prescribing no document
266	types or schemas.
267	
268	### 1.4 Principle statement formats
269	
270	TOGAF (The Open Group, TOGAF 9.2, "Architecture Principles" chapter, carried
271	into the 10th Edition ADM Techniques volume; pubs.opengroup.org) is, among the
272	sources this survey examined, the only broadly adopted formal template
273	specifically for principles: Name / Statement
274	(one-sentence unambiguous rule) / Rationale (business-language why) /
275	Implications (required actions and impacts), plus five quality criteria for
276	the set — Understandable, Robust (enables good decisions and enforceable
277	policies), Complete, Consistent, Stable (enduring but amendable under a change
278	process). The standard thus already pairs a construction definition with
279	derived quality criteria.
280	
281	Sentence-level normative language has two established conventions. IETF BCP 14
282	(RFC 2119, Bradner 1997; RFC 8174, Leiba 2017; datatracker.ietf.org) defines
283	MUST/SHOULD/MAY keyword families, restricts normative force to ALL-CAPS
284	(8174), requires an opt-in boilerplate, and rules that imperatives be used
285	sparingly and never to mandate implementation method. ISO/IEC Directives Part 2
286	(9th ed., 2021) binds one modal verb per provision type (shall=requirement,
287	should=recommendation, may=permission, can=possibility; "must" reserved for
288	external constraints), requires that requirements be objectively verifiable or
289	not stated as requirements, bans subjective qualifiers, and mandates an
290	explicit normative/informative split.
291	
292	Decision records are a distinct, established artifact kind: the Nygard ADR
293	(cognitect.com blog, 15 Nov 2011) — Title/Context/Decision/Status/Consequences,
294	value-neutral context, active-voice "We will…", consequences including
295	negatives, append-only numbering, supersede-never-rewrite, 1–2 pages; MADR
296	v4.0.0 (adr.github.io/madr, September 2024) — Markdown Architectural Decision
297	Records (corrected: v4.0.0 reverted the v3-era "Any Decision Records"
298	expansion) — adds Considered Options, Decision Drivers, an optional
299	Confirmation section stating how compliance will be verified, and YAML front
300	matter; and Y-statements (Zdun, Capilla, Tran, Zimmermann, "Sustainable
301	Architectural Design Decisions", IEEE Software 30(6), 2013,
302	doi:10.1109/MS.2013.97) — a one-sentence template whose clauses name the
303	rejected alternatives (canonically "neglected") and the accepted downside.
304	
305	Principle fitness criteria exist in the literature: Rumelt (Good Strategy Bad
306	Strategy, Crown Business, 2011) — a guiding policy "directs and constrains
307	action without fully defining it"; bad-strategy hallmarks fluff and
308	goals-mistaken-for-strategy; Spool ("Creating Great Design Principles: 6
309	Counter-intuitive Tests", UIE, March 2011; articles.centercentre.com) —
310	evidence-derived, helps-you-say-no, distinguishes-from-competitors,
311	reversible-in-context, per-project revalidated, meaning-calibrated-on-real-work;
312	Lencioni ("Make Your Values Mean Something", HBR 80(7), July 2002) — core vs
313	aspirational vs permission-to-play vs accidental values. Trade-off grammars:
314	the Agile Manifesto value pairs with the right-side-still-has-value qualifier
315	(agilemanifesto.org, 2001) and even/over statements — good-vs-good pairs with
316	declared priority (Dignan, Brave New Work, Portfolio/Penguin, 2019; Kamer,
317	"Even/Over Statements", The Ready on Medium, 2021). Operated exemplars: the
318	W3C TAG Web Platform Design Principles (w3ctag.github.io/design-principles;
319	living note, updated June 2026) — imperative titles with parenthetical stable
320	names, prose, worked examples, applied in actual spec reviews — and the GOV.UK
321	Government Design Principles (gov.uk, 2012, updated April 2025; now 11
322	principles), an amend-in-place principle set with public revision history.
323	
324	### 1.5 Content-quality guideline and rubric formats
325	
326	Educational assessment supplies the descriptor-rubric family: Brookhart (How
327	to Create and Use Rubrics, ASCD, 2013) — criteria about the quality of the
328	work, crossed with 3–5 prose performance-level descriptors of observable
329	features (not evaluative adjectives); analytic (per-criterion judgment) vs
330	holistic (single judgment) variants. The AAC&U VALUE rubrics (aacu.org/value/
331	rubrics; 15 rubrics developed 2007–2009, a 16th added 2013 — corrected) are a
332	fully worked, operated artifact set: Definition + Framing Language + Glossary preamble,
333	then a criteria-by-levels matrix with named ordered levels Capstone /
334	Milestones / Benchmark, with an explicit localization instruction. The
335	single-point rubric (Fluckiger, Delta Kappa Gamma Bulletin 76(4), 2010)
336	authors only the proficient-standard column, with blank flanking columns for
337	observed shortfalls and excesses.
338	
339	Binary gates: the Scrum DoD (2020 Scrum Guide) — one uniform itemized quality
340	contract with a consequence rule; acceptance criteria in scenario-oriented
341	Given/When/Then form (Gherkin; cucumber.io/docs/gherkin; Adzic, Specification
342	by Example, Manning, 2011) or rule-oriented list form; and checklist design
343	constraints from Gawande (The Checklist Manifesto, Metropolitan Books, 2009)
344	and the Gawande/Boorman "Checklist for Checklists" (projectcheck.org):
345	DO-CONFIRM vs READ-DO typing, named pause points, 5–9 killer items, ~60–90
346	second budget, field validation. Fagan inspections (IBM Systems Journal 15(3),
347	1976; Brykczynski's checklist survey, ACM SIGSOFT SEN 24(1), 1999) derive and
348	continuously re-derive checklist items from observed defect data.
349	
350	Quality taxonomies: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 (SQuaRE product quality model) — nine
351	characteristics decomposed into defined sub-characteristics, deliberately a
352	vocabulary separated from measures (2502n) and requirements (25030).
353	
354	Style-guide governance: the Google developer documentation style guide
355	(developers.google.com/style, public since September 2017) and the Microsoft
356	Writing Style Guide (learn.microsoft.com/style-guide, 2018–present) converge on
357	one anatomy — voice principles, a condensed highlights/top-10 layer, topical
358	rule pages with before/after examples, an A–Z word list, and an explicit
359	precedence hierarchy (project sheet → this guide → named fallbacks). The Vale
360	prose linter (vale.sh; LWN, "Vale: enforcing style guidelines for text", 2024)
361	mechanizes such guides: each YAML rule carries a check pattern, a severity
362	tier, and a link back to the guideline it enforces, packaged per style guide
363	with per-project overrides — checks derived from definitions, running in the
364	wild.
365	
366	Two architectural devices recur: Deming's operational definition (Out of the
367	Crisis, MIT Press, 1986, ch. 9) — a quality adjective has "no communicable
368	meaning" until expressed as sampling/test procedure + criterion + yes/no
369	decision rule; and WCAG 2.2's conformance architecture (W3C Recommendation, 5
370	Oct 2023) — principles → guidelines → 86 individually testable success criteria
371	(A:31, AA:24, AAA:31; corrected — 4.1.1 Parsing was removed as obsolete, so the
372	commonly repeated 87/A:32 count is wrong), with a strict normative/informative
373	split: criteria bind, Understanding and Techniques documents inform. Google's
374	code-review guidance (google.github.io/eng-practices) is a two-layer review
375	rubric: one senior decision principle (approve once the change "definitely
376	improves the overall code health," even if imperfect) plus an enumerated aspect
377	list, with authority routing (style → style guide/linter; design → principles).
378	The Federal Plain Language Guidelines (PLAIN, 2011, pursuant to the Plain
379	Writing Act of 2010, Pub. L. 111-274; originally plainlanguage.gov/guidelines,
380	now hosted at digital.gov/guides/plain-language — corrected URL) contribute the
381	imperative one-behavior-per-rule granularity with before/after example pairs.
382	
383	### 1.6 Quality-management lineage: document control, improvement loops, derivation trees
384	
385	This is the one surveyed tradition whose core artifact is the controlled
386	definition itself. ISO 9001:2015 clause 7.5 (Quality management systems —
387	Requirements; iso.org/standard/62085.html — current edition, confirmed 2021,
388	revision in progress; clause detail cross-verified via the official ISO/TC
389	176/SC2/N1286 guidance, iso.org/iso/documented_information.pdf, the standard
390	text itself being paywalled) is the established requirements regime for
391	controlled documents. The 2015 edition merged "documents" and "records" into
392	one concept, documented information, with two verbs carrying the old
393	distinction: maintain (keep current — definitional documents) vs retain (keep
394	as evidence — records). Clause 7.5.1 scopes the regime two ways — information
395	the standard requires plus whatever the organization determines necessary,
396	extent proportional to organization size, process complexity, and competence.
397	7.5.2 requires on creation and update: identification and description (title,
398	date, author, reference number), format and media, and review and approval
399	for suitability and adequacy. 7.5.3 requires that information be available
400	and suitable for use where and when needed and adequately protected, with
401	control activities as applicable: distribution, access (view-only vs
402	view-and-change), retrieval and use, storage and preservation including
403	legibility, control of changes (version control named explicitly), retention
404	and disposition; documented information of external origin is identified and
405	controlled, and information retained as evidence of conformity is protected
406	from unintended alteration. (The 2008 edition's explicit
407	prevent-unintended-use-of-obsolete-documents provision, 4.2.3(g), survives in
408	2015 only by implication of availability plus change control — corrected: an
409	earlier pass read it as explicit 2015 text.) Beneath it, ISO 9000:2015
410	(Fundamentals and vocabulary, 4th ed., September 2015;
411	iso.org/standard/45481.html) supplies the term system: document =
412	"information and the medium on which it is contained" (3.8.5); documented
413	information (3.8.6); record = "document stating results achieved or providing
414	evidence of activities performed" (3.8.10); conformity = fulfilment of a
415	requirement; objective evidence as the admissibility condition; and the
416	verification/validation split — confirmation via objective evidence that
417	specified requirements are fulfilled vs that requirements for a specific
418	intended use are fulfilled. ISO 10013:2021 (Guidance for documented
419	information, 1st ed., March 2021; iso.org/standard/75736.html) is the
420	non-binding how-to companion, updated for digitized documentation and
421	automated workflow; the traditional documentation-hierarchy pyramid (policy →
422	procedure → work instruction → form/record) belongs to its predecessor
423	ISO/TR 10013:2001 — the 2021 foreword states "the original hierarchy of
424	documentation is no longer used but left open for the user" (corrected: an
425	earlier pass attributed the pyramid to the 2021 edition).
426	
427	The improvement-loop lineage is documented end-to-end in Moen, "Foundation
428	and History of the PDSA Cycle" (Associates in Process Improvement;
429	deming.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/PDSA_History_Ron_Moen.pdf; retrieved in
430	full for this report). Shewhart (Statistical Method from the Viewpoint of
431	Quality Control, The Graduate School, USDA, 1939, p. 45; edited by Deming) is
432	the original statement that specification precedes production precedes
433	inspection, and that the line closes into a loop: "These three steps must go
434	in a circle instead of in a straight line... specification, production, and
435	inspection correspond respectively to making a hypothesis, carrying out an
436	experiment, and testing the hypothesis." Deming's 1950 JUSE wheel (design
437	with tests → make → sell → test in service through market research →
438	redesign) was recast by Japanese executives as Plan–Do–Check–Act (Imai,
439	Kaizen, Random House, 1986, p. 60; Ishikawa, What Is Total Quality Control?
440	The Japanese Way, Prentice-Hall, 1985, pp. 56–61 — Plan subdivided into goals
441	plus methods, Do into training plus implementation). PDCA's terminal phase is
442	a document-control action: Act is "back to plan if the results are
443	unsatisfactory, or standardization if the results are satisfactory"; the form
444	"emphasized the prevention of error recurrence by establishing standards and
445	the ongoing modification of those standards" (Moen), with Ishikawa adding
446	that standards are revised continuously from consumer voices and next-process
447	requirements; in Japanese practice loop turns are documented in the QC-story
448	format (Lillrank & Kano 1989, per Moen). Deming himself held his cycle apart
449	from PDCA ("They bear no relation to each other", GAO roundtable 1980; "be
450	sure to call it PDSA, not the corruption PDCA", letter to Moen, 17 November
451	1990): PDSA (Out of the Crisis, MIT Press, 1986, p. 88; The New Economics,
452	MIT Press, 1993, p. 135) plans a change with a stated prediction and its
453	theory (Moen, Nolan, Provost, Improving Quality Through Planned
454	Experimentation, McGraw-Hill, 1991, p. 11), runs it — small-scale, per the
455	1993 cycle figure — Studies observed results against the prediction (not
456	"Check", which Deming read as "hold back"), and then adopts, abandons, or
457	re-runs under changed conditions. The Model for Improvement (Langley, Nolan,
458	Nolan, "The Foundation of Improvement", Quality Progress, June 1994, p. 81;
459	Langley et al., The Improvement Guide, 2nd ed., Jossey-Bass, 2009, p. 24)
460	frames every cycle with three questions, the second — "How will we know that
461	a change is an improvement?" — an explicit check-derivation question. Moen's
462	division of labor: PDCA for implementation and compliance; PDSA for testing
463	and learning.
464	
465	Six Sigma contributes the qualitative-to-checkable derivation tree and the
466	phase-gated improvement process. The CTQ (critical-to-quality) tree — CTQs
467	being, in paraphrase of the ASQ Quality Glossary entry, the key measurable
468	characteristics of a product or process whose performance standards must be
469	met to satisfy the customer (asq.org/quality-resources/quality-glossary;
470	handbook treatment in Kubiak & Benbow, The Certified Six Sigma Black Belt
471	Handbook, 3rd ed., ASQ Quality Press, 2016; GE-lineage practice in Pande,
472	Neuman & Cavanagh, The Six Sigma Way, McGraw-Hill, 2000; matrix ancestor
473	Hauser & Clausing, "The House of Quality", HBR 66(3), May–June 1988, pp.
474	63–73; no single primary inventor source exists for the tree itself) —
475	derives in three fixed levels: a need stated in the customer's qualitative
476	language; the drivers by which the customer will judge the need met; and
477	per-driver measurable performance requirements, each with a specification
478	limit or target. Leaves must be measurable or the derivation is unfinished;
479	every leaf traces up through a driver to a stated need; and coverage is
480	testable in both directions (a need with no leaves is unmeasured, a leaf with
481	no need is unauthorized). DMAIC (ASQ, asq.org/quality-resources/dmaic; Kubiak
482	& Benbow 2016, organized to the DMAIC-structured ASQ Body of Knowledge)
483	specifies five phases by their exit deliverables: Define (charter, voice of
484	customer and CTQs, process map), Measure (baseline, operational definitions
485	of the measures, measurement-system validation — before any judgment of the
486	process), Analyze (root causes verified with data), Improve (solutions
487	validated against the baseline), Control (control plan, process standardized
488	into controlled documentation, monitoring installed, ownership transferred).
489	Phase boundaries carry tollgate reviews — phase deliverables reviewed by an
490	authority seat distinct from the performing team (sponsor/champion/Master
491	Black Belt) before the next phase is authorized; the tollgate form is
492	standard in the Six Sigma practice literature rather than on the cited ASQ
493	page. The Control-phase termination rule converges with PDCA's Act: in this
494	lineage, improvement work terminates in a document-control action on a
495	governed surface.
496	
497	### 1.7 Qualitative fitness-test formats for LLM output
498	
499	The research base: Zheng et al., "Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and
500	Chatbot Arena" (NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2306.05685) established LLM-judge viability
501	(>80% agreement with humans) and named position, verbosity, and
502	self-enhancement bias, with mitigations (position swap, reference-guided
503	grading, chain-of-thought). Zheng et al., "Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks"
504	(ICLR 2025 oral; arXiv:2410.07137) proved judges are adversarially gameable: a
505	constant null-model response reached 86.5% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0.
506	G-Eval (Liu et al., EMNLP 2023; arXiv:2303.16634) canonized the derivation
507	procedure criteria → evaluation steps → judged score (Spearman 0.514 on
508	summarization). EvalGen (Shankar et al., UIST 2024; arXiv:2404.12272)

IBM Systems Journal 24(2), 1985, pp. 79–90) is the lightest classic
per-activity frame: Entry criteria, Task set, Validation conditions, eXit
criteria per activity cell, composable by chaining, with no ordering engine.
(Corrected: the original expansion is Validation, not Verification; both
renderings circulate in CMM-lineage secondary literature. A free scan exists at
bitsavers.org despite the IBM Systems Journal paywall.) The frame places
validation conditions inside the activity definition cell itself.

OMG Essence 1.2 (SEMAT; OMG formal/18-10-02, 2018; omg.org/spec/Essence —
1.2 remains the current formal version; Essence 2.0 is still an in-process
beta, its beta 2 published March 2026 and not yet formally published as of
August 2026, per the OMG specification page — corrected) defines
progress and health rather than workflow: Alphas (essential trackable concerns)
with ordered named states, each state carrying a short qualitative checklist;
activities whose completion criteria are expressed in terms of alpha states and
work-product levels of detail — a definition-level termination semantic
requiring no engine; competencies with five levels; practice/method
composition; a card presentation format.

CMMI contributes a structural trichotomy: in CMMI for Development V1.3
(CMU/SEI-2010-TR-033, 2010) goals are required components, practices are
expected, and subpractices/example work products are informative — appraisal
targets goal achievement, not practice performance; CMMI V3.0 (ISACA, 2023)
recasts this as practice areas with intent and value statements and
evolutionary practice-group levels. ITIL v3 (Service Design, 2011 ed., Cabinet
Office/TSO) documents every process in one fixed section skeleton (purpose/
objectives, scope, value, policies, activities, triggers/inputs/outputs/
interfaces, CSFs with nested KPIs, risks), and ITIL 4 (AXELOS, 2019; 34
practice guides) does the same for practices — success factors and metrics
nested under the definition.

Notation standards exist but describe flow or I/O, not construction quality:
BPMN 2.0 (OMG formal/2011-01-03; ISO/IEC 19510:2013, which is technically BPMN
2.0.1) with its Descriptive vs Analytic vs Common Executable conformance
sub-classes; CMMN 1.0/1.1 (OMG, 2014; Marin, arXiv:1608.05011) — declarative
case plans with sentries (entry/exit criteria), milestones, and discretionary
items, addressed to case work whose activities cannot be fully pre-sequenced;
IDEF0 (NIST FIPS PUB 183, 1993, withdrawn as a federal
standard in 2008; IEEE 1320.1-1998; ISO/IEC/IEEE 31320-1:2012) with its
Input/Control/Output/Mechanism arrow typing; and PMBOK 6th ed. ITTOs (PMI,
2017), which the PMBOK 7th ed. (2021) itself dropped from the core. ISO/IEC
24744:2014 (SEMDM) models method-level and endeavor-level views of one concept
via powertypes; this survey found no practitioner process corpus written in it
comparable to the 15288/12207 corpus, the application literature encountered
being academic method-engineering work (observation from this research pass,
not a cited measurement).

### 1.2 Role definition formats

OMG SPEM 2.0 (formal/2008-04-01, April 2008; omg.org/spec/SPEM/2.0) draws a
hard structural line between Method Content — reusable Role Definitions
(skills, responsibilities), Task Definitions, Work Product Definitions, typed
Guidance including checklists — and Process, which arranges content occurrences
into lifecycles. A full knowledge base of role/task/artifact definitions can be
maintained without ever creating a process. Eclipse EPF Composer
(projects.eclipse.org/projects/technology.epf; archived, last release 2018)
implements the split in tooling: method plugins publish role/task/work-product/guidance pages
as a browsable static site, no engine. RUP (Kruchten, The Rational Unified
Process: An Introduction, 3rd ed., Addison-Wesley, 2003, ch. 3) is the
ancestor form: roles carry responsibilities plus required competencies, and
every artifact has exactly one responsible role.

The Scrum Guide (Schwaber & Sutherland, November 2020, scrumguides.org) defines
roles as short accountability lists — 4–8 bullets of what the holder is
answerable for, not task scripts.

Responsibility assignment across roles has its own established forms, distinct
from the definition containers above. The responsibility assignment matrix
(RAM) and its common type, the RACI chart, are carried in the PMBOK Guide: a
RAM is "a grid that shows the project resources assigned to each work
package"; a RACI chart is "a common type of RAM that uses responsible,
accountable, consult, and inform statuses to define the involvement of
stakeholders in project activities" (PMI, PMBOK Guide, 6th ed., 2017, §9.1
data-representation tools and glossary — definitions confirmed via
PMI-affiliated PMP literature quoting the Guide, the Guide itself being
paywalled; ancestry in the Linear Responsibility Chart, Cleland & King,
Systems Analysis and Project Management, McGraw-Hill, 1968). The matrix
crosses work items (rows) with roles (columns), one involvement status per
cell. The one-Accountable-per-row rule — exactly one A per deliverable — is
stated as hard doctrine throughout PMI-affiliated practitioner literature,
though the PMBOK glossary itself defines only the four statuses; the R-A-C-I
lettering has no documented originator (folklore attributions to GE/1950s are
unverified). Practitioner criticism records recurring failure modes: multiple
As dissolving accountability, R/A conflation, team-level unnamed assignments,
consulted-list bloat, and shelfware charts drafted once and never consulted
(e.g. tallyfy.com/raci-matrix — criticism in circulation, not authority).
Letter-set variants extend the cell vocabulary on the same skeleton: RASCI
(S = Support, splitting doer from helper), RACI-VSL (V = Verifier against
acceptance criteria, S = Signatory), CAIRO (O = explicitly Omitted), RACIQ
(Q = Quality review), PARIS (variant inventory per the Wikipedia RAM article,
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsibility_assignment_matrix). A decision-rights
fork re-targets the matrix from tasks to decisions: Bain's RAPID — Recommend /
Agree / Perform / Input / Decide, "one person who must decide — the single
point of accountability", plus a four-locus taxonomy of decision bottlenecks
(Rogers & Blenko, "Who Has the D?", HBR 84(1), January 2006;
bain.com/insights/who-has-the-d/) — and DACI — Driver / Approver /
Contributors / Informed, one Approver, splitting process ownership (Driver)
from final authority (Approver) (Atlassian Team Playbook,
atlassian.com/team-playbook/plays/daci; the commonly repeated Intuit-1980s
origin is an unverified secondary attribution).

Holacracy constitutionalizes the role definition itself (Holacracy
Constitution v5.0, holacracy.org/constitution/5-0; source text at
github.com/holacracyone/Holacracy-Constitution, CC BY-SA 4.0; Robertson,
Holacracy, Henry Holt, 2015). Its §1.1 defines a Role as a descriptive name
plus three optional typed parts: Purpose ("a capacity, potential, or goal that
the Role will pursue or express"), Domains (things the role exclusively
controls and regulates as its property), and Accountabilities ("ongoing
activities the Role will manage and enact in service of others"), by
documented HolacracyOne convention phrased as gerunds. Role and person are
strictly separated: a person filling a role is its Role Lead (§1.2), assigned
by a Circle Lead (§1.4.1), many-to-many in both directions. Definitions change
only through the governance process (Article 5): proposals must be grounded in
a concrete tension with an example (§5.3.1), are processed by integrative
decision-making (§5.4.5), and objections must pass defined validity tests
(§5.3.2–5.3.3); amendments are recorded, giving the role set an audit trail.
A documented exit exists: Medium abandoned Holacracy in 2016, reporting that
"the act of codifying responsibilities in explicit detail hindered a proactive
attitude and sense of communal ownership" (Doyle, "Management and Organization
at Medium", Medium blog, 4 March 2016).

Team Topologies (Skelton & Pais, IT Revolution, 2019; concept definitions at
teamtopologies.com/key-concepts) types teams — stream-aligned, enabling,
complicated-subsystem, platform — and types the relationship between any two
teams into three interaction modes: collaboration ("working together for a
defined period of time to discover new things"), X-as-a-Service ("one team
provides and one team consumes something 'as a Service'"), and facilitating
("one team helps and mentors another team"), with a designed evolution —
collaboration is deliberately time-bounded and expected to decay into
X-as-a-Service as interfaces stabilize. It is the one surveyed form that types
role-to-role interaction rather than involvement in a deliverable.

In current agent practice, the Claude Code subagent definition
(code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) is a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter
is the delegation and capability contract (required name and description;
optional tools/disallowedTools, model, maxTurns, skills preload list, memory
scope) and whose body is the role's standing system prompt. The shop already
uses this container for lead-po and lead-architect.

### 1.3 Artifact / document-type schema formats

ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289:2019 (Content of life-cycle information items, 4th ed.;
earlier editions 2011/2015/2017; iso.org/standard/74909.html) is the
established meta-format: every information item is classified as one of seven
generic document types — description, plan, policy, procedure, report, request,
specification — each generic type carrying generic content requirements, and
each named item carrying specific required-content clauses. It is explicitly
medium-independent, and its mapping tables tie information items to the
12207/15288 processes that produce and consume them.

RUP artifacts (Kruchten 2003, ch. 3) ship with templates and checkpoints —
per-artifact review checklists attached to the artifact definition. The 2020
Scrum Guide pairs every artifact with exactly one commitment (Product Backlog →
Product Goal, Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal, Increment → Definition of Done);
the DoD is "a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets
the quality measures required for the product," with a defined consequence:
non-conforming work returns to the Product Backlog. Microsoft Prompty
(prompty.ai/core-concepts/file-format; microsoft/prompty) demonstrates a
schema-validated asset format whose frontmatter declares inputs, outputs, and
per-input sample/default data. The MCP resources primitive (Model Context
Protocol spec 2025-06-18) standardizes inclusion-decision metadata on context
artifacts: audience, priority 0.0–1.0, lastModified.

Two traditions govern how document kinds themselves are derived and bounded.
DITA 1.3 (OASIS Standard, 17 December 2015; Errata 02, 2018;
docs.oasis-open.org/dita/dita/v1.3) types every topic as one of a small set of
information types sharing one structural envelope (title + prolog metadata +
body): the base triad concept / task / reference, extended in the 1.3
technical-content set by glossaryEntry (introduced in DITA 1.1 — corrected: an
earlier research pass dated it to 1.3) and troubleshooting (the type actually
new in 1.3). Typing exists to "keep documentation focused and modular"; mixing
information types within one topic is the named anti-pattern; and a document's
root element must be <topic> or a specialization, <map> or a specialization,
or <dita> (corrected: <dita> is also a permitted root). Maps — separate
documents that "organize topics and other resources into structured
collections" — carry hierarchy, inter-topic relationships, and key-resolution
context, so organization is fully separated from content. DITA's
specialization architecture (archSpec "Specialization"; the definition sits in
the spec's terminology section) is a governed derivation mechanism: "defining
new element or attribute types as a semantic refinement of existing element or
attribute types". Every specialized type declares its full ancestry (@class),
so a processor that knows only the base type can still process the derived one
(generic fallback); vocabulary compatibility between documents is decidable
(@domains); each type is declared in exactly one vocabulary module; and
constraint modules restrict an existing type's content model as a distinct,
lighter operation than creating a new type (fallback and constraint rules
specified in adjacent archSpec sections).

Diátaxis (Procida, diataxis.fr; authorship per the site's colophon — the
homepage does not name the author) classifies on an axis orthogonal to
15289's content genres: by the user's need at the moment of use. Two axes —
action/cognition crossed with acquisition/application ("at work" vs "at
study") — generate exactly four types: tutorial, how-to guide, reference,
explanation. The type determines "documentation content (what to write),
style (how to write it) and architecture (how to organise it)"; the named
failure mode is the blurring or collapse of the forms into one document,
which the site prescribes keeping apart (an each-document-serves-one-type
rule in paraphrase — the site states it as failure-mode avoidance, not in
those words). Adjacent: arc42 (Hruschka & Starke, arc42.org, in practice
since 2005) is a fixed 12-section skeleton for one composite artifact kind —
the architecture description — with explicit tailoring permission and a
decision-record slot (its section 9) embedding the ADR kind by reference; and
docs-as-code (Write the Docs, writethedocs.org/guide/docs-as-code; Gentle,
Docs Like Code) names the substrate practice — documentation in plain-text
markup under version control, peer-reviewed via the code-review mechanism,
gated by automated tests in CI — while deliberately prescribing no document
types or schemas.

### 1.4 Principle statement formats

TOGAF (The Open Group, TOGAF 9.2, "Architecture Principles" chapter, carried
into the 10th Edition ADM Techniques volume; pubs.opengroup.org) is, among the
sources this survey examined, the only broadly adopted formal template
specifically for principles: Name / Statement
(one-sentence unambiguous rule) / Rationale (business-language why) /
Implications (required actions and impacts), plus five quality criteria for
the set — Understandable, Robust (enables good decisions and enforceable
policies), Complete, Consistent, Stable (enduring but amendable under a change
process). The standard thus already pairs a construction definition with
derived quality criteria.

Sentence-level normative language has two established conventions. IETF BCP 14
(RFC 2119, Bradner 1997; RFC 8174, Leiba 2017; datatracker.ietf.org) defines
MUST/SHOULD/MAY keyword families, restricts normative force to ALL-CAPS
(8174), requires an opt-in boilerplate, and rules that imperatives be used
sparingly and never to mandate implementation method. ISO/IEC Directives Part 2
(9th ed., 2021) binds one modal verb per provision type (shall=requirement,
should=recommendation, may=permission, can=possibility; "must" reserved for
external constraints), requires that requirements be objectively verifiable or
not stated as requirements, bans subjective qualifiers, and mandates an
explicit normative/informative split.

Decision records are a distinct, established artifact kind: the Nygard ADR
(cognitect.com blog, 15 Nov 2011) — Title/Context/Decision/Status/Consequences,
value-neutral context, active-voice "We will…", consequences including
negatives, append-only numbering, supersede-never-rewrite, 1–2 pages; MADR
v4.0.0 (adr.github.io/madr, September 2024) — Markdown Architectural Decision
Records (corrected: v4.0.0 reverted the v3-era "Any Decision Records"
expansion) — adds Considered Options, Decision Drivers, an optional
Confirmation section stating how compliance will be verified, and YAML front
matter; and Y-statements (Zdun, Capilla, Tran, Zimmermann, "Sustainable
Architectural Design Decisions", IEEE Software 30(6), 2013,
doi:10.1109/MS.2013.97) — a one-sentence template whose clauses name the
rejected alternatives (canonically "neglected") and the accepted downside.

Principle fitness criteria exist in the literature: Rumelt (Good Strategy Bad
Strategy, Crown Business, 2011) — a guiding policy "directs and constrains
action without fully defining it"; bad-strategy hallmarks fluff and
goals-mistaken-for-strategy; Spool ("Creating Great Design Principles: 6
Counter-intuitive Tests", UIE, March 2011; articles.centercentre.com) —
evidence-derived, helps-you-say-no, distinguishes-from-competitors,
reversible-in-context, per-project revalidated, meaning-calibrated-on-real-work;
Lencioni ("Make Your Values Mean Something", HBR 80(7), July 2002) — core vs
aspirational vs permission-to-play vs accidental values. Trade-off grammars:
the Agile Manifesto value pairs with the right-side-still-has-value qualifier
(agilemanifesto.org, 2001) and even/over statements — good-vs-good pairs with
declared priority (Dignan, Brave New Work, Portfolio/Penguin, 2019; Kamer,
"Even/Over Statements", The Ready on Medium, 2021). Operated exemplars: the
W3C TAG Web Platform Design Principles (w3ctag.github.io/design-principles;
living note, updated June 2026) — imperative titles with parenthetical stable
names, prose, worked examples, applied in actual spec reviews — and the GOV.UK
Government Design Principles (gov.uk, 2012, updated April 2025; now 11
principles), an amend-in-place principle set with public revision history.

### 1.5 Content-quality guideline and rubric formats

Educational assessment supplies the descriptor-rubric family: Brookhart (How
to Create and Use Rubrics, ASCD, 2013) — criteria about the quality of the
work, crossed with 3–5 prose performance-level descriptors of observable
features (not evaluative adjectives); analytic (per-criterion judgment) vs
holistic (single judgment) variants. The AAC&U VALUE rubrics (aacu.org/value/
rubrics; 15 rubrics developed 2007–2009, a 16th added 2013 — corrected) are a
fully worked, operated artifact set: Definition + Framing Language + Glossary preamble,
then a criteria-by-levels matrix with named ordered levels Capstone /
Milestones / Benchmark, with an explicit localization instruction. The
single-point rubric (Fluckiger, Delta Kappa Gamma Bulletin 76(4), 2010)
authors only the proficient-standard column, with blank flanking columns for
observed shortfalls and excesses.

Binary gates: the Scrum DoD (2020 Scrum Guide) — one uniform itemized quality
contract with a consequence rule; acceptance criteria in scenario-oriented
Given/When/Then form (Gherkin; cucumber.io/docs/gherkin; Adzic, Specification
by Example, Manning, 2011) or rule-oriented list form; and checklist design
constraints from Gawande (The Checklist Manifesto, Metropolitan Books, 2009)
and the Gawande/Boorman "Checklist for Checklists" (projectcheck.org):
DO-CONFIRM vs READ-DO typing, named pause points, 5–9 killer items, ~60–90
second budget, field validation. Fagan inspections (IBM Systems Journal 15(3),
1976; Brykczynski's checklist survey, ACM SIGSOFT SEN 24(1), 1999) derive and
continuously re-derive checklist items from observed defect data.

Quality taxonomies: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 (SQuaRE product quality model) — nine
characteristics decomposed into defined sub-characteristics, deliberately a
vocabulary separated from measures (2502n) and requirements (25030).

Style-guide governance: the Google developer documentation style guide
(developers.google.com/style, public since September 2017) and the Microsoft
Writing Style Guide (learn.microsoft.com/style-guide, 2018–present) converge on
one anatomy — voice principles, a condensed highlights/top-10 layer, topical
rule pages with before/after examples, an A–Z word list, and an explicit
precedence hierarchy (project sheet → this guide → named fallbacks). The Vale
prose linter (vale.sh; LWN, "Vale: enforcing style guidelines for text", 2024)
mechanizes such guides: each YAML rule carries a check pattern, a severity
tier, and a link back to the guideline it enforces, packaged per style guide
with per-project overrides — checks derived from definitions, running in the
wild.

Two architectural devices recur: Deming's operational definition (Out of the
Crisis, MIT Press, 1986, ch. 9) — a quality adjective has "no communicable
meaning" until expressed as sampling/test procedure + criterion + yes/no
decision rule; and WCAG 2.2's conformance architecture (W3C Recommendation, 5
Oct 2023) — principles → guidelines → 86 individually testable success criteria
(A:31, AA:24, AAA:31; corrected — 4.1.1 Parsing was removed as obsolete, so the
commonly repeated 87/A:32 count is wrong), with a strict normative/informative
split: criteria bind, Understanding and Techniques documents inform. Google's
code-review guidance (google.github.io/eng-practices) is a two-layer review
rubric: one senior decision principle (approve once the change "definitely
improves the overall code health," even if imperfect) plus an enumerated aspect
list, with authority routing (style → style guide/linter; design → principles).
The Federal Plain Language Guidelines (PLAIN, 2011, pursuant to the Plain
Writing Act of 2010, Pub. L. 111-274; originally plainlanguage.gov/guidelines,
now hosted at digital.gov/guides/plain-language — corrected URL) contribute the
imperative one-behavior-per-rule granularity with before/after example pairs.

### 1.6 Quality-management lineage: document control, improvement loops, derivation trees

This is the one surveyed tradition whose core artifact is the controlled
definition itself. ISO 9001:2015 clause 7.5 (Quality management systems —
Requirements; iso.org/standard/62085.html — current edition, confirmed 2021,
revision in progress; clause detail cross-verified via the official ISO/TC
176/SC2/N1286 guidance, iso.org/iso/documented_information.pdf, the standard
text itself being paywalled) is the established requirements regime for
controlled documents. The 2015 edition merged "documents" and "records" into
one concept, documented information, with two verbs carrying the old
distinction: maintain (keep current — definitional documents) vs retain (keep
as evidence — records). Clause 7.5.1 scopes the regime two ways — information
the standard requires plus whatever the organization determines necessary,
extent proportional to organization size, process complexity, and competence.
7.5.2 requires on creation and update: identification and description (title,
date, author, reference number), format and media, and review and approval
for suitability and adequacy. 7.5.3 requires that information be available
and suitable for use where and when needed and adequately protected, with
control activities as applicable: distribution, access (view-only vs
view-and-change), retrieval and use, storage and preservation including
legibility, control of changes (version control named explicitly), retention
and disposition; documented information of external origin is identified and
controlled, and information retained as evidence of conformity is protected
from unintended alteration. (The 2008 edition's explicit
prevent-unintended-use-of-obsolete-documents provision, 4.2.3(g), survives in
2015 only by implication of availability plus change control — corrected: an
earlier pass read it as explicit 2015 text.) Beneath it, ISO 9000:2015
(Fundamentals and vocabulary, 4th ed., September 2015;
iso.org/standard/45481.html) supplies the term system: document =
"information and the medium on which it is contained" (3.8.5); documented
information (3.8.6); record = "document stating results achieved or providing
evidence of activities performed" (3.8.10); conformity = fulfilment of a
requirement; objective evidence as the admissibility condition; and the
verification/validation split — confirmation via objective evidence that
specified requirements are fulfilled vs that requirements for a specific
intended use are fulfilled. ISO 10013:2021 (Guidance for documented
information, 1st ed., March 2021; iso.org/standard/75736.html) is the
non-binding how-to companion, updated for digitized documentation and
automated workflow; the traditional documentation-hierarchy pyramid (policy →
procedure → work instruction → form/record) belongs to its predecessor
ISO/TR 10013:2001 — the 2021 foreword states "the original hierarchy of
documentation is no longer used but left open for the user" (corrected: an
earlier pass attributed the pyramid to the 2021 edition).

The improvement-loop lineage is documented end-to-end in Moen, "Foundation
and History of the PDSA Cycle" (Associates in Process Improvement;
deming.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/PDSA_History_Ron_Moen.pdf; retrieved in
full for this report). Shewhart (Statistical Method from the Viewpoint of
Quality Control, The Graduate School, USDA, 1939, p. 45; edited by Deming) is
the original statement that specification precedes production precedes
inspection, and that the line closes into a loop: "These three steps must go
in a circle instead of in a straight line... specification, production, and
inspection correspond respectively to making a hypothesis, carrying out an
experiment, and testing the hypothesis." Deming's 1950 JUSE wheel (design
with tests → make → sell → test in service through market research →
redesign) was recast by Japanese executives as Plan–Do–Check–Act (Imai,
Kaizen, Random House, 1986, p. 60; Ishikawa, What Is Total Quality Control?
The Japanese Way, Prentice-Hall, 1985, pp. 56–61 — Plan subdivided into goals
plus methods, Do into training plus implementation). PDCA's terminal phase is
a document-control action: Act is "back to plan if the results are
unsatisfactory, or standardization if the results are satisfactory"; the form
"emphasized the prevention of error recurrence by establishing standards and
the ongoing modification of those standards" (Moen), with Ishikawa adding
that standards are revised continuously from consumer voices and next-process
requirements; in Japanese practice loop turns are documented in the QC-story
format (Lillrank & Kano 1989, per Moen). Deming himself held his cycle apart
from PDCA ("They bear no relation to each other", GAO roundtable 1980; "be
sure to call it PDSA, not the corruption PDCA", letter to Moen, 17 November
1990): PDSA (Out of the Crisis, MIT Press, 1986, p. 88; The New Economics,
MIT Press, 1993, p. 135) plans a change with a stated prediction and its
theory (Moen, Nolan, Provost, Improving Quality Through Planned
Experimentation, McGraw-Hill, 1991, p. 11), runs it — small-scale, per the
1993 cycle figure — Studies observed results against the prediction (not
"Check", which Deming read as "hold back"), and then adopts, abandons, or
re-runs under changed conditions. The Model for Improvement (Langley, Nolan,
Nolan, "The Foundation of Improvement", Quality Progress, June 1994, p. 81;
Langley et al., The Improvement Guide, 2nd ed., Jossey-Bass, 2009, p. 24)
frames every cycle with three questions, the second — "How will we know that
a change is an improvement?" — an explicit check-derivation question. Moen's
division of labor: PDCA for implementation and compliance; PDSA for testing
and learning.

Six Sigma contributes the qualitative-to-checkable derivation tree and the
phase-gated improvement process. The CTQ (critical-to-quality) tree — CTQs
being, in paraphrase of the ASQ Quality Glossary entry, the key measurable
characteristics of a product or process whose performance standards must be
met to satisfy the customer (asq.org/quality-resources/quality-glossary;
handbook treatment in Kubiak & Benbow, The Certified Six Sigma Black Belt
Handbook, 3rd ed., ASQ Quality Press, 2016; GE-lineage practice in Pande,
Neuman & Cavanagh, The Six Sigma Way, McGraw-Hill, 2000; matrix ancestor
Hauser & Clausing, "The House of Quality", HBR 66(3), May–June 1988, pp.
63–73; no single primary inventor source exists for the tree itself) —
derives in three fixed levels: a need stated in the customer's qualitative
language; the drivers by which the customer will judge the need met; and
per-driver measurable performance requirements, each with a specification
limit or target. Leaves must be measurable or the derivation is unfinished;
every leaf traces up through a driver to a stated need; and coverage is
testable in both directions (a need with no leaves is unmeasured, a leaf with
no need is unauthorized). DMAIC (ASQ, asq.org/quality-resources/dmaic; Kubiak
& Benbow 2016, organized to the DMAIC-structured ASQ Body of Knowledge)
specifies five phases by their exit deliverables: Define (charter, voice of
customer and CTQs, process map), Measure (baseline, operational definitions
of the measures, measurement-system validation — before any judgment of the
process), Analyze (root causes verified with data), Improve (solutions
validated against the baseline), Control (control plan, process standardized
into controlled documentation, monitoring installed, ownership transferred).
Phase boundaries carry tollgate reviews — phase deliverables reviewed by an
authority seat distinct from the performing team (sponsor/champion/Master
Black Belt) before the next phase is authorized; the tollgate form is
standard in the Six Sigma practice literature rather than on the cited ASQ
page. The Control-phase termination rule converges with PDCA's Act: in this
lineage, improvement work terminates in a document-control action on a
governed surface.
